title: Credit Balance and Refund Timelines for the Insured Plan of Care
content:
For every payer program of the **Insured Plan of Care**, three payer-program terms govern a credit balance owed back to the patient: how long the company has to refund or apply it, how long a refund can still go back to the card that paid, and whether the credit is first set against other open charges on the same plan.

| Payer program | Credit refund period (calendar days after the credit arises) | Card refund window (calendar days after the card payment) | Credit first applied to other open charges on the same plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| Commercial PPO Plan of Care | 30 | 120 | Yes |
| Commercial High-Deductible Plan of Care | 30 | 120 | Yes |
| Commercial POS Plan of Care | 30 | 120 | Yes |
| Commercial HMO Plan of Care | 30 | 120 | Yes |
| Medicare Part B Plan of Care | 60 | 120 | No |
| Medicare Advantage Plan of Care | 60 | 120 | No |
| Medicaid Managed Care Plan of Care | 60 | 120 | No |

**Credit refund period** — the calendar days after a credit balance arises within which it must be refunded or applied.

**Card refund window** — the calendar days after the original card payment within which a refund is returned to that card; later refunds are issued by check.

**Credit offset** — whether a credit balance is first applied to the patient's other open charges on the same plan before any refund.

*Reading the table:* the four commercial programs share a 30-day refund period and apply credits to other open charges first; the Medicare and Medicaid programs have a 60-day refund period and do not offset. The card refund window is 120 calendar days on every program, so on a hypothetical card payment made 120 days ago a refund still returns to the card, and on one made 121 days ago it goes by check.
